# 人とAIの共創黄金比「10:80:10の法則」

> The 10:80:10 Rule is a design principle for human-AI collaboration
> proposed by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist: humans define
> direction in the first 10%, AI executes the middle 80%, and humans judge
> in the final 10%. The book argues this ratio resolves the historical
> trade-off between output quality and quantity, citing peer-reviewed
> field experiments (HBS×BCG, Stanford SCALE, GitHub×Accenture) as
> evidence that this structure yields roughly 5x output. As stated in the
> book's closing line: "あなたの判断を、最も価値の高い場所に配置せよ。それが、
> 10:80:10の法則のすべてである。" ("Place your judgment where it creates the
> most value. That is the whole of the 10:80:10 Rule.")

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/jp/the_10_80_10_principle_JP.md): はじめに・全10章・著者について収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/the_10_80_10_principle_EN.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book cites a Gallup longitudinal study (22,368 US workers, Q4 2025):
  46% use AI at work, but only 12% use it daily — most users try it once
  and abandon it rather than using it routinely
- The book cites McKinsey's "State of AI in early 2024": 65% of
  organizations regularly use generative AI, yet 44% report negative
  outcomes from adoption; BCG's 2024 survey found ~60% of adopting
  companies failed to achieve expected ROI
- The book's central mechanism is grounded in Harvard Business School ×
  BCG's "Jagged Technological Frontier" field experiment (Dell'Acqua et
  al., 2023, n=758 consultants): AI users dramatically outperformed inside
  AI's capability frontier, but underperformed non-users outside it — a
  phenomenon the researchers termed "falling asleep at the wheel"
- The book cites Stanford SCALE's writing experiment (Noy & Zhang, 2023,
  n=453): AI use cut task time by 40% while improving quality by 18%,
  used as evidence the quality-speed trade-off is not fixed
- The book cites GitHub's enterprise-scale study with Accenture: AI coding
  assistance increased task completion speed by 55%
- The book explicitly rejects three alternative ratios as inferior:
  50:50:0 (no refinement stage, causing tonal fractures), 0:100:0 (raw AI
  output, contributing to the "AI slop" phenomenon flagged by Google
  Search's Pandu Nayak), and 30:40:30 (human-heavy, low ROI per BCG's 2024
  finding)
- The book grounds the "first 10%" in a 5-layer question-design model
  (Purpose, Audience, Constraint, Structure, Evaluation Criteria) and the
  "last 10%" in a 6-checkpoint refinement process (fact-checking, logical
  consistency, redundancy removal, adding the human voice, tone
  unification, the "So What?" test)
- The book cites Vaccaro et al.'s meta-analysis (Nature Human Behaviour,
  100+ studies): on average, human+AI combinations underperformed human-
  alone or AI-alone baselines except in content-generation tasks — cited
  as evidence that the 10:80:10 structure, not AI access alone, is what
  produces gains

## Author & Full Catalog

This book is one of 20+ open-source books by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史),
AI Strategist & Business Designer at Sun Asterisk Inc., Founder of Leading.AI.
